newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Siemens unit to tap postal sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Siemens unit to tap postal sales.

text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG said on Wednesday its automation unit would see bigger sales this year and a sharp increase in the next 10, largely because of a newly-acquired postal systems business.
Siemens Automation (AUT) expects AEG Electrocom GmbH to provide almost all its growth in the 1996/97 business year, unit president Manfred von Raven told a news conference.

Electrocom, bought from Daimler-Benz AG earlier this month, would also help drive international growth -- which AUT is counting on to lift sales more than 50 percent to 10 billion marks ($6.1 billion) over the next decade, Raven said.
"This acquisition will add standard letter-sorting systems to AUT's range of postal logistics products and will clearly strengthen our position, mainly in countries outside Europe," he said.

Without Electrocom, which had 1995 sales of about one billion marks ($609 million) with about 70 percent coming from the United States, AUT's 1996/97 sales and profit would remain stable in 1996/97 and show no noticeable improvement in 1997/98, he said.

The flat forecast for the next two years, a change from earlier forecasts, parallels the Siemens group outlook for no earnings improvement in the current business year, analysts who follow Siemens said.

"AUT is seeing the same trend as the rest of Siemens," said Heinz Steffen of Kleinwort Benson Research in Frankfurt. "But I think it can continue to be one of Siemens' strongest units and the AEG acquisition will help."
In 1995/96, which ended on September 30, AUT was one of Siemens' most profitable units, reporting 6.6 billion marks in sales and 509 million marks in pretax profit.
Over the next 10 years, AUT aims for 10 billion marks in sales and a seven percent return on sales, Raven said.
Electrocom should play a key role in that climb by increasing orders, Raven said.

"A new major focus has arisen in the international growth market for postal logistics where we have been able to obtain contracts for large letter-sorting plants in Germany, the Netherlands, the U.S. and recently China," he said.
Industrial automation products, such as machine tools and systems that assemble circuit boards, would also drive international growth, Raven said.
In China, where Siemens has a joint venture with the China North Industries Group, sales of numerical control machine tools should at least double to 24,000 units in five years, he said.

Prospects were also strong in the U.S., where orders rose 38 percent last year to 520 million marks. European orders rose 20 percent last year to 490 million marks, although German orders remained flat at four billion marks, Raven said.
